text.p: Zaire's veteran president, Mobutu Sese Seko, returned home on Tuesday to a rapturous welcome after four months in Europe where he had surgery for prostate cancer, witnesses said.

Up to 20,000 people gathered at the international airport in the capital Kinshasa to welcome home the man whose supporters describe him as the one symbol of unity in the anarchic Central African nation gripped by a revolt in the east.
Witnesses said Mobutu, 66, smiled broadly as he walked down the steps from the aircraft with his wife to be met by cheering, drumming and singing from around the airport.
He walked unaided and easily, carrying his trade-mark carved walking stick.
Mobutu has dominated the life of the nation since seizing power in 1965. He bowed to foreign and domestic pressure for democratic reforms in 1990 but elections have yet to be held.
Mobutu has announced his intention to stand for elected office once the elections finally take place. Under the transitional constitution, this must now be before July 1997.
